body: I'll reopen it, since it's probably best to fix this in the setup script

pip install for sqlalchemy fails on docker debian:unstable. To reproduce:
```
apt update
apt install python3 python3-dev python3-pip
python3 -m pip install sqlalchemy 
````
I got that part.  but why?  what is non-compliant about our setup.py ?

I'm not sure. Maybe a new version of setup tools enables pep 517 by default?

It may just be that setup.py needs to opt-out of pep517?
It's not setuptools that enables pep517, it's pip that calls PEP517 backend.
@CaselIT is that the full log? Usually, when that breaks it has another exception from the subprocess.
that is the log running pip with the verbose output
I'm pretty sure that pip/python's broken there.
Also, the best way to fight this is to publish OS-specific wheels matrix so that building from source won't be triggered.

that was also my thought. Since it seems that it's using pep517 from `/usr/share/python-wheels/`, but I've yet to test if reinstalling pep517 with pip helps.

it may be that the python package in debian unstable is broken

I've tried reinstalling pip with `python3 -m pip install -I pip` and the sqlalchemy successfully installs so I think that the problem is in the debian version installed with apt. 

Also reading https://twitter.com/codewithanthony/status/1240690187543298048
>debian's wheel hacks are broken again (any from-source pep517 package breaks in the same way).  the presence of pyproject.toml (even though it's just for black) is triggering pip to do that.  a workaround is `pip install --no-use-pep517`

Seems to suggest that pyproject.toml may be why pip tries to use pep517. 
We could maybe exclude it from the archive on pypi.

Closing this. Thank for the help @webknjaz
we cant build wheels because SQLAlchemy includes native code and we dont have the resources to maintain native builds for all OSes.
